1	# JS Framework Benchmark: 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	
     5	The **JS Framework Benchmark** is the most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause and hosted on GitHub, it measures operations such as creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping, removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled CPU throttling.
     6	
     7	Since its inception, the project has published **over 60 official result sets**, covering Chrome versions from **55 (circa 2017) all the way to 146 (mid-2026)**. Each result set captures dozens of frameworks — both keyed and non-keyed implementations — giving developers a consistent yardstick for performance.
     8	
     9	## Methodology Milestones
    10	
    11	The benchmark has undergone several important methodology changes that make **cross-version comparisons unreliable**:
    12	
    13	| Milestone | Chrome Version | Year | Description |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| Weighted Geometric Mean | 118 | 2023 | Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean |
    16	| CPU Throttling Adjustment | 118 | 2023 | Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation |
    17	| Measurement Fine-Tuning | 118+ | 2023–present | Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation |
    18	| Keyed-Only Alternation | 139+ | 2025–2026 | Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only |
    19	
    20	Because of these evolving parameters, the project explicitly warns: *"Comparisons across Chrome versions aren't always safe since the benchmark and its driver are constantly developing."*
    21	
    22	## Timeline of Official Runs
    23	
    24	The table below summarizes the distribution of official benchmark runs by year:
    25	
    26	| Year | Chrome Versions | Number of Runs | Notes |
    27	|---|---|---|---|
    28	| 2017–2019 | 55, 58, 62, 69 | 4 | Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net |
    29	| 2020 | 83 – 87 | 5 | Migrated to GitHub Pages |
    30	| 2021 | 88 – 96 | 9 | Steady monthly cadence established |
    31	| 2022 | 97 – 108 | 13 | Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104) |
    32	| 2023 | 109 – 120 | 12 | Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118 |
    33	| 2024 | 121 – 131 | 12 | Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121) |
    34	| 2025 | 132 – 143 | 12 | Most active year; alternating keyed-only runs |
    35	| 2026 | 144 – 146 | 3 (so far) | Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS |
    36	
    37	## Platform Coverage
    38	
    39	The vast majority of runs — **over 95%** — were executed on **macOS (OSX)**. Only two Windows-specific runs exist:
    40	
    41	- **Chrome 104 – Windows** (2022)
    42	- **Chrome 121 – Windows** (2024)
    43	
    44	This means the benchmark primarily reflects macOS + Chrome performance characteristics.
    45	
    46	## Key Takeaways for Developers
    47	
    48	1. **Compare within the same Chrome version.** Methodology and throttling differ across releases.
    49	2. **Consult the latest run** (currently Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.
    50	3. **Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.** Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs benchmark keyed frameworks only, while even-numbered runs include both.
    51	4. **60+ data points over 8 years** make this the longest-running, most comprehensive JS framework performance tracker available.
    52	5. **Weighted geometric mean** (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score than the previous arithmetic approach.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a dark-mode, data-forward poster for the JS Framework Benchmark.
A1 portrait: 594 x 841 mm at 150 dpi -> 3508 x 4961 px
"""

import os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Canvas setup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DPI = 150
MM_TO_INCH = 0.0393701
WIDTH_MM = 594
HEIGHT_MM = 841
WIDTH = int(WIDTH_MM * MM_TO_INCH * DPI)   # 3508
HEIGHT = int(HEIGHT_MM * MM_TO_INCH * DPI) # 4961

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Palette & fonts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BG = "#0B1120"          # deep navy
PANEL = "#111827"       # slightly lighter panel bg
ACCENT_BLUE = "#38BDF8" # electric blue
ACCENT_TEAL = "#2DD4BF" # teal
ACCENT_AMBER = "#F59E0B"# amber warning
TEXT_MAIN = "#F8FAFC"   # near-white
TEXT_MUTED = "#94A3B8"  # slate-400
GRID = "#1E293B"        # subtle grid lines
BORDER = "#334155"      # slate-700

# Load fonts
font_mono = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf", 24)
font_mono_sm = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf", 20)
font_mono_xs = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf", 16)
font_sans = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", 36)
font_sans_sm = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", 28)
font_sans_xs = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", 22)
font_sans_bold = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 42)
font_sans_bold_lg = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 56)
font_sans_bold_xl = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 90)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def draw_rounded_rect(draw, xy, radius, fill, outline=None, width=1):
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = xy
    draw.rounded_rectangle(xy, radius=radius, fill=fill, outline=outline, width=width)

def text_size(draw, text, font):
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]

def draw_centered_text(draw, text, font, color, cx, cy):
    w, h = text_size(draw, text, font)
    draw.text((cx - w // 2, cy - h // 2), text, font=font, fill=color)

def draw_right_text(draw, text, font, color, rx, cy):
    w, h = text_size(draw, text, font)
    draw.text((rx - w, cy - h // 2), text, font=font, fill=color)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
timeline_data = [
    ("2017", "55", 4, "Early era"),
    ("2018", "58–62", 2, ""),
    ("2019", "69", 1, ""),
    ("2020", "83–87", 5, "GitHub Pages"),
    ("2021", "88–96", 9, "Monthly cadence"),
    ("2022", "97–108", 13, "2 Windows runs"),
    ("2023", "109–120", 12, "Methodology overhaul at 118"),
    ("2024", "121–131", 12, "1 Windows run"),
    ("2025", "132–143", 12, "Most active year"),
    ("2026", "144–146", 3, "Latest: Chrome 146"),
]

metrics = [
    ("Total Official\nBenchmark Runs", "60+", "Chrome 55 → 146"),
    ("Chrome Versions\nCovered", "55 – 146", "~8 years of releases"),
    ("Scoring Method\nChanged At", "Chrome 118", "Weighted geometric mean"),
    ("Primary\nPlatform", "macOS", "Only 2 Windows runs"),
    ("Runs in\n2025 Alone", "12", "Chrome 132–143"),
]

milestones = [
    ("Weighted Geometric Mean", "Chrome 118", "Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean"),
    ("CPU Throttling Adjustment", "Chrome 118", "Throttling factors recalibrated for realistic load simulation"),
    ("Measurement Fine-Tuning", "Chrome 118+", "Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation"),
    ("Keyed-Only Alternation", "Chrome 139+", "Odd versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only"),
]

takeaways = [
    "Compare within the same Chrome version — methodology and throttling differ across releases.",
    "Consult the latest run (Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.",
    "Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes: odd Chrome runs = keyed only; even = both.",
    "60+ data points over 8 years make this the longest-running JS framework performance tracker.",
    "Weighted geometric mean (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score.",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main canvas
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
img = Image.new("RGB", (WIDTH, HEIGHT), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Background dot grid
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
for y in range(0, HEIGHT, 40):
    for x in range(0, WIDTH, 40):
        draw.point((x, y), fill=GRID)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Header
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
header_h = 380
# subtle top accent bar
draw.rectangle([0, 0, WIDTH, 8], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
# title
draw.text((80, 60), "JS FRAMEWORK BENCHMARK", font=font_sans_bold_lg, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.text((80, 140), "5 Years of Browser Performance Testing", font=font_sans, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
# one-liner
draw.text((80, 220), "A comprehensive overview of the official JavaScript web framework benchmark", font=font_sans_sm, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((80, 270), "spanning Chrome 55 through Chrome 146, tracking methodology and ecosystem evolution.", font=font_sans_sm, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hero stats bar
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
stats_y = 340
stats_h = 220
panel_margin = 60
panel_w = (WIDTH - panel_margin * 2 - 40) // 5
for i, (label, value, ctx) in enumerate(metrics):
    x = panel_margin + i * (panel_w + 10)
    draw_rounded_rect(draw, (x, stats_y, x + panel_w, stats_y + stats_h), 12, PANEL, BORDER, 1)
    # value
    val_w, val_h = text_size(draw, value, font_sans_bold_xl)
    # scale down if too wide
    fval = font_sans_bold_xl
    if val_w > panel_w - 20:
        fval = font_sans_bold_lg
        val_w, val_h = text_size(draw, value, fval)
    draw.text((x + (panel_w - val_w) // 2, stats_y + 30), value, font=fval, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
    # label
    lines = label.split("\n")
    ly = stats_y + 120
    for line in lines:
        lw, lh = text_size(draw, line, font_mono_sm)
        draw.text((x + (panel_w - lw) // 2, ly), line, font=font_mono_sm, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
        ly += lh + 4
    # context
    cw, ch = text_size(draw, ctx, font_mono_xs)
    draw.text((x + (panel_w - cw) // 2, stats_y + stats_h - 40), ctx, font=font_mono_xs, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timeline section
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
section_y = stats_y + stats_h + 50
section_title = "BENCHMARK TIMELINE: CHROME 55 → CHROME 146"
draw.text((80, section_y), section_title, font=font_sans_bold, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.rectangle([80, section_y + 55, WIDTH - 80, section_y + 57], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)

timeline_y = section_y + 90
timeline_h = 260
row_h = 44
col_xs = [80, 260, 520, 780, 1100]
col_titles = ["Year", "Chrome Versions", "Runs", "Notes"]

# table header bg
draw.rectangle([80, timeline_y, WIDTH - 80, timeline_y + row_h], fill="#1E293B")
for cx, ct in zip(col_xs, col_titles):
    draw.text((cx + 10, timeline_y + 8), ct, font=font_mono_sm, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)

# rows
for idx, (year, versions, runs, note) in enumerate(timeline_data):
    ry = timeline_y + row_h + idx * row_h
    bgc = PANEL if idx % 2 == 0 else BG
    draw.rectangle([80, ry, WIDTH - 80, ry + row_h], fill=bgc)
    # highlight 2023 row for Chrome 118
    if year == "2023":
        draw.rectangle([80, ry, WIDTH - 80, ry + row_h], outline=ACCENT_AMBER, width=2)
        # amber warning pill
        pill_text = "⚠ METHODOLOGY CHANGE"
        pw, ph = text_size(draw, pill_text, font_mono_xs)
        px = WIDTH - 80 - pw - 30
        py = ry + 8
        draw.rounded_rectangle([px, py, px + pw + 20, py + ph + 8], radius=6, fill="#451a03", outline=ACCENT_AMBER, width=1)
        draw.text((px + 10, py + 4), pill_text, font=font_mono_xs, fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
    draw.text((col_xs[0] + 10, ry + 8), year, font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
    draw.text((col_xs[1] + 10, ry + 8), versions, font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
    draw.text((col_xs[2] + 10, ry + 8), str(runs), font=font_mono, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
    draw.text((col_xs[3] + 10, ry + 8), note, font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Methodology Milestones
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
meth_y = timeline_y + row_h + len(timeline_data) * row_h + 70
meth_title = "METHODOLOGY MILESTONES"
draw.text((80, meth_y), meth_title, font=font_sans_bold, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.rectangle([80, meth_y + 55, WIDTH - 80, meth_y + 57], fill=ACCENT_AMBER)

meth_content_y = meth_y + 90
meth_card_w = (WIDTH - 80 * 2 - 30) // 2
meth_card_h = 160
for idx, (title, version, desc) in enumerate(milestones):
    col = idx % 2
    row = idx // 2
    x = 80 + col * (meth_card_w + 30)
    y = meth_content_y + row * (meth_card_h + 20)
    draw_rounded_rect(draw, (x, y, x + meth_card_w, y + meth_card_h), 14, PANEL, BORDER, 1)
    # version badge
    badge = version
    bw, bh = text_size(draw, badge, font_mono_sm)
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x + 20, y + 20, x + 20 + bw + 20, y + 20 + bh + 10], radius=6, fill="#1e3a8a", outline=ACCENT_BLUE, width=1)
    draw.text((x + 30, y + 25), badge, font=font_mono_sm, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
    # title
    draw.text((x + 20, y + 70), title, font=font_sans_sm, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
    # desc
    draw.text((x + 20, y + 115), desc, font=font_mono_sm, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Coverage & Keyed/Non-keyed mini section
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cov_y = meth_content_y + 2 * (meth_card_h + 20) + 70
cov_title = "PLATFORM & FRAMEWORK COVERAGE"
draw.text((80, cov_y), cov_title, font=font_sans_bold, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.rectangle([80, cov_y + 55, WIDTH - 80, cov_y + 57], fill=ACCENT_TEAL)

cov_content_y = cov_y + 90
cov_card_w = (WIDTH - 80 * 2 - 30) // 2
cov_card_h = 200

# Left: Platform
x = 80
y = cov_content_y
draw_rounded_rect(draw, (x, y, x + cov_card_w, y + cov_card_h), 14, PANEL, BORDER, 1)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 30), "PLATFORM BREAKDOWN", font=font_sans_sm, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
# macOS bar
bar_w = cov_card_w - 60
bar_h = 24
mac_w = int(bar_w * 0.95)
draw.rounded_rectangle([x + 30, y + 90, x + 30 + bar_w, y + 90 + bar_h], radius=4, fill=GRID)
draw.rounded_rectangle([x + 30, y + 90, x + 30 + mac_w, y + 90 + bar_h], radius=4, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 60), "macOS (OSX)", font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.text((x + 30 + mac_w + 10, y + 88), ">95%", font=font_mono_sm, fill=ACCENT_TEAL)
# Windows bar
win_w = int(bar_w * 0.05)
draw.rounded_rectangle([x + 30, y + 130, x + 30 + bar_w, y + 130 + bar_h], radius=4, fill=GRID)
draw.rounded_rectangle([x + 30, y + 130, x + 30 + win_w, y + 130 + bar_h], radius=4, fill=ACCENT_AMBER)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 160), "Windows", font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((x + 30 + win_w + 10, y + 128), "2 runs", font=font_mono_sm, fill=ACCENT_AMBER)

# Right: Keyed vs Non-keyed
x = 80 + cov_card_w + 30
y = cov_content_y
draw_rounded_rect(draw, (x, y, x + cov_card_w, y + cov_card_h), 14, PANEL, BORDER, 1)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 30), "KEYED VS NON-KEYED RUNS", font=font_sans_sm, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 80), "Even Chrome versions", font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 110), "→ Full benchmark (keyed + non-keyed)", font=font_mono_sm, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 150), "Odd Chrome versions (139+)", font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.text((x + 30, y + 180), "→ Keyed frameworks only", font=font_mono_sm, fill=TEXT_MUTED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Key Takeaways
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
take_y = cov_content_y + cov_card_h + 70
take_title = "KEY TAKEAWAYS FOR DEVELOPERS"
draw.text((80, take_y), take_title, font=font_sans_bold, fill=TEXT_MAIN)
draw.rectangle([80, take_y + 55, WIDTH - 80, take_y + 57], fill=ACCENT_BLUE)

take_content_y = take_y + 90
for idx, txt in enumerate(takeaways):
    y = take_content_y + idx * 60
    # bullet
    draw.rounded_rectangle([80, y + 10, 100, y + 30], radius=4, fill=ACCENT_BLUE)
    draw.text((120, y + 4), txt, font=font_mono, fill=TEXT_MAIN)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Footer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
footer_y = HEIGHT - 100
draw.rectangle([0, footer_y, WIDTH, HEIGHT], fill=PANEL)
draw.text((80, footer_y + 30), "Source: github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark  ·  Data: Chrome 55 – 146 (2017–2026)", font=font_mono_xs, fill=TEXT_MUTED)
draw_right_text(draw, "Generated 2026-05-01", font_mono_xs, TEXT_MUTED, WIDTH - 80, footer_y + 40)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
out_path = "/app/output/final_poster.png"
img.save(out_path, "PNG")
print(f"Saved poster to {out_path} ({WIDTH}x{HEIGHT})")

- **Platform & Framework Coverage** — split panel with a 95 % macOS vs 2 Windows runs bar chart, plus a keyed vs non-keyed explanation.

The layout is clean, monospaced for data labels, sans-serif for headings, and structured like an engineering dashboard.
